At least 10 people were massacred in raids on three villages around the city of Beni, in North Kivu, in the early hours of Wednesday morning.

rfi.title: Hegseth urges Europe to counter migrant 'invasion' in D-Day anniversary speech
rfi.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has urged European countries to confront what he described as an “invasion” of their coastlines by migration, using a D-Day anniversary speech in Normandy to press both cultural and security arguments central to President Donald Trump’s administration.

rfi.title: Bernadette Chirac, France’s formidable former first lady, dies aged 93
rfi.description: Bernadette Chirac, the formidable former first lady of France who spent 12 years at the Élysée Palace beside President Jacques Chirac while forging her own political identity and transforming a children’s hospital charity into a national institution, has died aged 93.

rfi.title: Pope Leo XIV visits Spain as Church seeks a fresh voice in changing Europe
rfi.description: Pope Leo XIV has begun a weeklong visit to Spain, bringing the American pontiff to one of Europe’s historic centres of Christianity at a moment of political tension, social change and renewed curiosity about faith.

rfi.title: Teen queen Andreeva crushes Chwalinska to claim her first French Open crown
rfi.description: Nineteen-year-old Mirra Andreeva swept past qualifier Maja Chwalinska on Saturday to claim her first French Open title.

rfi.title: Could tackling climate change and levelling inequality go hand in hand?
rfi.description: The world can raise income, reduce inequality and limit global warming, according to an ambitious roadmap presented this week by economists in France. Making the case for a radical transformation of economies and lifestyles, they call on rich countries to slow growth, phase out fossil fuels and tax the wealthiest to help poorer countries fund development and mitigate the effects of climate change.

rfi.title: Turkey expands influence in Africa through military training
rfi.description: Turkey is expanding its military training programmes across Africa, with soldiers from Mali and Niger graduating from a special forces camp as Ankara seeks to deepen ties across the continent.

rfi.title: US Ebola facility in Kenya fuels anger in a country with no cases
rfi.description: With no recorded cases of Ebola, many Kenyans are struggling to understand why their government is allowing the United States to build an Ebola facility in their country to treat US citizens. Despite protests and criticism, the Kenyan government has vowed to press on.

rfi.title: Africa's finest: Senegal, runners-up with something to prove
rfi.description: Senegal enter the first 48-team World Cup as Africa's second best side in the Fifa rankings. In the sixth instalment of a nine-part series on African squads at the tournament, RFI looks at a nation making its fourth appearance fresh from heartbreak at the continent's Cup of Nations.

rfi.title: Mali junta puts €3m bounty on Sahel al-Qaeda leader Ag Ghali
rfi.description: Mali's military government has offered a €3 million reward for information that leads to the arrest or killing of Iyad Ag Ghali, head of the Sahel branch of al-Qaeda that launched a major offensive in April.

rfi.title: French sons of slave traders and enslaved unite to seek a path to justice
rfi.description: In Nantes, France's largest slave port, the descendant of a slave-trading family has joined forces with a man whose ancestors were enslaved to help repair the enduring legacy of slavery from the grassroots up.

rfi.title: South Africa unrest grows as migrants become ‘scapegoats’
rfi.description: South Africa is once again facing a rise in anti-migrant tensions, with vigilante groups reportedly going door to door demanding that undocumented foreign nationals leave the country by the end of June. Post-apartheid specialist Cécile Perrot tells RFI the violence reflects deeper social and economic problems and that migrants have increasingly become scapegoats for poverty and unemployment.

rfi.title: France questions judicial system after girl's suspected murder
rfi.description: France's government was on Friday assessing possible judicial failings, after allegations that investigators could have prevented a 11-year-old girl's disappearance by better dealing with previous sexual abuse complaints.

rfi.title: Zverev sees off Mensik to reach French Open final
rfi.description: Second seed Alexander Zverev beat the 26th seed Jakub Mensik in four sets on Friday to advance to the men's singles final at the French Open in Paris where he will play 10th seed Flavio Cobolli.

rfi.title: Dozens dead of thirst after truck breaks down in Niger desert
rfi.description: Forty-nine people died of dehydration in a remote part of the Sahara desert in north-west Niger after the truck transporting them broke down, authorities said on Thursday.

rfi.title: French billionaire Stérin reveals far-right agenda in first public hearing
rfi.description: French billionaire Pierre-Edouard Stérin has used his first appearance before lawmakers to lay bare his "meta-political" campaign to bring free-market and conservative ideas into power to battle "socialism, wokism, Islamism and immigration", less than a year before France’s presidential election.

rfi.title: Diallo gives Cote d'Ivoire shock win over France, just days before World Cup
rfi.description: Amad Diallo scored a late winner as Cote d'Ivoire stunned France 2-1 in a World Cup warm-up match in Nantes on Thursday.

rfi.title: Western Balkan leaders join EU summit amid renewed enlargement drive
rfi.description: EU and Western Balkan leaders are gathering in the Adriatic port town of Tivat in Montenegro on Friday, alongside heads of Europe's largest economies including French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

rfi.title: Hungary drops charges against organisers of banned Pride marches
rfi.description: Hungarian prosecutors said Thursday they had dropped charges against organisers of last year's Pride marches, citing a landmark ruling from the EU's top court.

euronews.title: D-Day 82nd anniversary honoured in France
euronews.description: World leaders and the last remaining veterans gathered in Normandy on Saturday to mark the 82nd anniversary of the D-Day landings. Commemorations in Langrune-sur-Mer and Colleville-sur-Mer paid tribute to the 160,000 Allied troops who launched the liberation of Europe in 1944.

euronews.title: Google rents SpaceX/AI supercomputers for $920M a month, ahead of IPO
euronews.description: Google has signed a $30 billion deal to lease computing power from SpaceX, paying $920 million per month through June 2029. The move came after SpaceX acquired xAI in February 2026, gaining massive data centres. The deal precedes SpaceX’s highly anticipated IPO next week.

euronews.description: Pope Leo XIV set foot on Spanish soil on Saturday 6 June, ending a fifteen‑year papal absence. Over 130,000 people greeted him in Madrid, where he warned against ready‑made ideologies and called for reconciliation.

euronews.description: Newlyweds Dua Lipa and Callum Turner were seen greeting guests and celebrating at a wedding party in Palermo, Sicily, as part of a weekend of festivities following their recent London wedding.

euronews.description: Iran's players have received US visas ahead of the World Cup, but several federation officials are still awaiting clearance before the team's opening match.

euronews.title: Lazio Maremma cowboys: tradition and innovation at Canale Monterano's Riarto
euronews.description: For centuries, the buttero was central to livestock and rural life in the Maremma between Lazio and Tuscany. Though the trade is fading, new horsemen keep the region's history and identity alive.

lemonde.title: SFR racheté pour plus de 20 milliards d’euros par Bouygues Telecom, Free et Orange ; fortes inquiétudes sur l’emploi
lemonde.description: Patrick Drahi s’est entendu avec ses trois rivaux pour leur céder son groupe. SFR est donc appelé à disparaître si les autorités de concurrence donnent leur aval. Les salariés redoutent de perdre leur poste, dans un climat social déjà dégradé.

lemonde.title: A Paris, la maire du 10ᵉ arrondissement agressée par des « militants d’extrême droite » en marge de Nuit blanche
lemonde.description: Alexandra Cordebard dit avoir été « bousculée » et avoir « reçu des coups » donnés par des individus qui tentaient d’empêcher la présentation au public d’une œuvre dans l’église Saint-Laurent. L’édile et la mairie de Paris vont porter plainte.

lemonde.title: A Saint-Pétersbourg, le « Davos de Poutine » s’achève comme il a commencé, sous une pluie de drones ukrainiens
lemonde.description: La ville natale du président russe a été ciblée par plus d’une centaine de drones ukrainiens, samedi 6 juin, dernier jour du Forum économique international qui s’y tient chaque année. Présent sur place, la veille, Vladimir Poutine avait adressé une fin de non-recevoir au président ukrainien, Volodymyr Zelensky, qui lui avait proposé une rencontre en vue d’engager des pourparlers de paix.

lemonde.title: Bernadette Chirac, ancienne première dame, est morte à l’âge de 93 ans
lemonde.description: Indéfectible soutien de la carrière de son mari, Bernadette Chodron de Courcel était devenue un personnage incontournable de la scène politique. Elue au conseil général de Corrèze, très engagée dans l’action caritative, elle s’est éteinte, vendredi, à 93 ans.

lemonde.title: Roland-Garros 2026 : Mirra Andreeva a résisté à tous les vents contraires pour entrer dans le cercle des vainqueures en Grand Chelem
lemonde.description: La Russe de 19 ans s’est imposée, samedi, en finale, 6-3, 6-2, face à la surprise polonaise Maja Chwalinska. L’aboutissement d’une quinzaine durant laquelle la 8ᵉ joueuse mondiale a réussi à composer avec la pression, contrairement aux autres favorites.

lemonde.title: Le cinéaste israélien Nadav Lapid, visé par une polémique, renonce à participer au festival FID Marseille
lemonde.description: Plusieurs cinéastes avaient décidé de retirer leur film de la manifestation prévue en juillet pour protester contre la présence du réalisateur.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, Moyen-Orient : Israël dit avoir visé 150 sites liés au Hezbollah en deux jours dans le sud du Liban
lemonde.description: Dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi, l’Iran a tiré des missiles en direction de pays du Golfe, affirmant avoir « répondu de manière proportionnée » aux attaques américaines au titre de la légitime défense. Les Etats-Unis avaient dit, de leur côté, avoir « frappé des sites de radars de surveillance côtière iraniens » après avoir abattu des drones.

lemonde.title: « Personne n’était prêt pour ce qui allait se passer » : de retour d’une expédition à bord d’une flottille pour Gaza, une militante témoigne des violences subies
lemonde.description: La justice française a ouvert une enquête pour « tortures » et « crimes de guerre » à la suite d’un signalement du Quai d’Orsay sur la manière dont des Français de la flottille pour Gaza ont été traités par Israël. Malika Baouya, qui était à bord, raconte avoir été torturée par les militaires israéliens.

lemonde.title: Staffan Ingemar Lindberg, politologue : « Le recul démocratique qui s’observe au niveau mondial est inédit »
lemonde.description: Dans un entretien au « Monde », le fondateur suédois de l’institut Varieties of Democracy, qui publie chaque année un rapport sur l’état global de la démocratie, analyse les tendances actuelles.

lemonde.title: Free parties : à Rennes, des milliers de manifestants dénoncent « des propositions de loi liberticides »
lemonde.description: Quelques milliers de personnes ont défilé samedi à Rennes, en musique et derrière des camions diffusant de la musique techno, pour protester contre deux textes législatifs qui durciraient significativement les sanctions visant les organisateurs de free-parties et leur public.

lemonde.title: VIDEO. Le Real Madrid, la paix dans le monde et l’IA au menu de la première journée de visite de Leon XIV en Espagne
lemonde.description: Attendu à Madrid et aux îles Canaries pour un voyage centré sur les « droits humains », Léon XIV a dès son premier discours auprès de la famille royale espagnole appelée les dirigeants mondiaux à la paix.

lemonde.title: En Arménie, Samvel Karapetyan, le milliardaire venu de Russie qui rêve de prendre le pouvoir
lemonde.description: L’oligarque russo-arménien, candidat aux élections législatives de dimanche 7 juin, a reçu « Le Monde » chez lui à Erevan, où il est assigné à résidence depuis son arrestation en juin 2025. L’opposant au premier ministre, Nikol Pachinian, entend restaurer de « bonnes relations » avec Moscou.

lemonde.title: Y aller ou pas ? Le dilemme des artistes et des auteurs invités dans les villes RN
lemonde.description: Nombre d’acteurs du secteur s’interrogent sur leur participation à des événements dans des communes dirigées par l’extrême droite, qui mène une offensive culturelle.

lemonde.title: Le Centre présidentiel Obama va ouvrir ses portes à Chicago, au terme d’une saga de dix ans
lemonde.description: Déjà surnommé « l’Obamalisque » ou « l’œil de Sauron », l’édifice à l’allure de tour médiévale abrite un musée qui inscrit la présidence du premier président américain noir dans la continuité de luttes menées depuis la fin du XIXᵉ siècle.

lemonde.title: Le projet de loi contre l’antisémitisme et le racisme sera présenté le 1er juillet en conseil des ministres
lemonde.description: L’objectif est que le texte, qui prévoit notamment d’élargir le délit de négationnisme et d’introduire une peine d’inéligibilité pour certaines infractions, soit adopté avant la fin de l’année, selon la ministre déléguée chargée de la Lutte contre les discriminations.

lemonde.title: Bana Jabri, l’immunologiste qui veut protéger les bébés des maladies génétiques en testant les futurs parents
lemonde.description: A la tête de l’Institut Imagine, à Paris, depuis janvier 2025, la médecin chercheuse, qui a longtemps enseigné aux Etats-Unis, se mobilise pour que la prochaine loi sur la bioéthique autorise le dépistage préconceptionnel en population générale.

lemonde.title: A Carpentras, la nouvelle mairie RN supprime les subventions au Planning familial en invoquant « redoubler de rigueur dans sa gestion financière »

observador.description: Os riscos da “Shadow AI” não se limitam à fiabilidade técnica. Existe um problema ainda mais profundo: o impacto da utilização invisível de IA sobre os próprios fundamentos da função jurisdicional.

observador.title: Urânio!
observador.description: Albert Camus dizia que quem escreve de uma forma clara tem leitores e quem escreve de forma obscura tem comentadores. Espero que haja mais quem leia do que comente o livro “Urânio!” agora publicado.

observador.title: Abrir a Porta da Arena Não Basta
observador.description: Ou por que razão a verdadeira inclusão não pode viver apenas de quotas, percentagens e boas intenções.

observador.title: EUDR: o equívoco da palavra "simplificação"
observador.description: O EUDR continua a aplicar-se. A obrigação mudou de local; não desapareceu. As consequências para quem o ignorar continuam a ser as mesmas.

observador.title: Palavras ocas e braços cruzados: Açores
observador.description: O maior drama da juventude açoriana é viver numa terra onde estudar não garante futur e trabalhar não garante independência.

observador.title: Dos SMTUC à empresa intermunicipal: Coimbra
observador.description: Coimbra tem a oportunidade de transformar os SMTUC no principal instrumento público de mobilidade da região.

observador.title: EUA suspeitam que Israel tentou espiar negociações com Irão
observador.description: Um alto-funcionário entrevistado afirma que Israel sempre prosseguiu uma "recolha agressiva" de informações tanto de aliados quanto adversários, mas que atingiu um nível "descontrolado".

observador.title: Rolls melhora o eléctrico Spectre em potência e autonomia
observador.description: O Spectre, o primeiro eléctrico da Rolls-Royce e o segundo mais vendido da gama, foi alvo de um “boost”. Aumenta a potência dos seus dois motores e a autonomia, entre outros pormenores.

observador.title: Milhares protestam contra 'resort' da família Trump
observador.description: Os protestos contra este projeto, estimado em cerca de 4 mil milhões de euros e associado à filha de Donald Trump Ivanka e ao seu marido, Jared Kushner, estão a ganhar força neste país dos Balcãs.

observador.title: 23h. Portugal vence Chile por 2-1 em preparação para o Mundi
observador.description: Golos dos portugueses Gonçalo Guedes e Bruno Fernandes, ambos na segunda parte do jogo. Ainda, PCP acusa o Governo de marcar a discussão da reforma laboral "à má fila" por "medo".

observador.title: Assassinato de oito pessoas deixa Equador em choque
observador.description: Tinham entre 15 e 31 anos, alguns eram familiares mas nenhum tinha qualquer atividade relacionada com o tráfico de droga. Polícia procura responsáveis.

observador.title: O difícil travão que a Anthropic quer aplicar na IA
observador.description: "O Claude passou de super-prestável a super-humano em menos de um ano”, diz a Anthropic. Empresa teme sistemas que consigam criar sucessos autónomos, pedindo um abrandamento na IA.

observador.title: Tensão em reunião da Junta de Vila do Conde
observador.description: Eleitos do PS envolveram-se em empurrões e gritos com membros dos partidos da oposição: PSD, Chega e CDS.

observador.title: "Foi um jogo interessante, permitiu trabalhar várias coisas"
observador.description: Frente ao Chile, Leão foi expulso e pode falhar o primeiro jogo do Mundial, ao passo que Bruno Fernandes entrou no top 5 de melhores marcadores da Seleção. Martínez agradado com o triunfo.

observador.title: Meio milhão de pessoas celebra com o Papa em Madrid
observador.description: Leão XIV termina o primeiro dia da viagem no centro da capital espanhola, numa "vigília de oração com os jovens" em que estão 500 mil pessoas.

observador.title: Nuno Campos vai treinar o Dinamo de Bucareste
observador.description: "Bem-vindo, Nuno Campos! O nosso clube chegou a um acordo com o treinador lusitano para assumir o comando técnico", escreveu no Facebook o emblema da capital da Roménia.

spiegel.title: Deutschland in der Einzelkritik: Kai Havertz in WM-Form, Leroy Sané als Matchwinner
spiegel.description: Beim letzten Test vor der WM zeigen sich noch nicht alle deutschen Spieler in ihrer besten Verfassung. Während Keeper Oliver Baumann gegen die USA ein starker Neuer-Ersatz war, wackelte Nico Schlotterbeck. Die Einzelkritik.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Deutschland bei Sieg gegen die USA mit Problemen im letzten Test
spiegel.description: Gegen die USA gerät das DFB-Team in ungeahnte Turbulenzen, hatte mit dem WM-Gastgeber 45 Minuten lang große Probleme. Leroy Sané gelang erst wenig, dann das Siegtor. Bis zum Turnierstart muss sich die Mannschaft steigern.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Iran wirft USA »rachsüchtiges Verhalten« vor
spiegel.description: Das iranische Fußballteam hat Visa für die WM in den USA bekommen. Doch 14 Mitarbeiter und Funktionäre sind leer ausgegangen. Iran sieht sich dadurch sportlich benachteiligt.

spiegel.title: Pete Hegseth nahm bei offizieller Europareise sechs seiner Kinder mit
spiegel.description: US-Verteidigungsminister Hegseth hat seine Frau und sechs seiner sieben Kinder zu einer Gedenkfeier für den D-Day mitgenommen. In seiner Rede in Frankreich verglich er Migration mit einer Invasion.

spiegel.title: Anthony Head ist tot: Eine der geliebtesten Heldenfiguren der Fernsehgeschichte
spiegel.description: Anthony Head verkörperte als Bibliothekar Giles in »Buffy« schon vor Jahrzehnten einen modernen Mann. Einen, der Macht abgab, weil er verstand, dass andere Menschen sie besser nutzen konnten.

spiegel.title: Andrew Tate reist nach Russland. Und seine mutmaßlichen Opfer warten auf Gerechtigkeit
spiegel.description: Wegen Vergewaltigungsvorwürfen müsste sich Andrew Tate eigentlich vor britischen Gerichten verantworten. Doch der Prozess kommt nicht voran – während Tate in Russland gefeiert wird.

spiegel.title: Fußball-Länderspiel: Deutschland schlägt die USA im letzten Test vor der WM
spiegel.description: Kai Havertz schoss die DFB-Elf in Chicago früh in Führung, danach tat sich Deutschland schwer. In der zweiten Hälfte traf dann Leroy Sané und sorgte für eine erfolgreiche Generalprobe. Die Partie im Minutenprotokoll.

spiegel.title: Pflege: Wie der Medizinische Dienst über Leistungen und Einstufung entscheidet
spiegel.description: Beate Jahn ist Gutachterin des Medizinischen Dienstes, von ihr hängt maßgeblich ab, ob jemand als pflegebedürftig gilt oder nicht. Jetzt sollen die Regeln verschärft werden. Unterwegs in einem System, dem das Geld ausgeht.

spiegel.title: Aktivisten servieren AfD-Politikern veganes Mett-Hakenkreuz
spiegel.description: Beim Frühstück im Hotel sind AfD-Politiker von einer politischen Botschaft überrascht worden: ein Hakenkreuz aus veganem Mett, garniert mit Gurken. Die Partei reagiert empört.

spiegel.title: Monaco: Kim Kardashian schon wieder in der Nähe von Lewis Hamilton
spiegel.description: In Paris, beim Super Bowl, beim Coachella-Festival: Kim Kardashian und Formel-1-Star Lewis Hamilton haben sich zuletzt auffallend oft getroffen. Nun hat er sie beim Großen Preis von Monaco sogar ins Fahrerlager eingeladen.

spiegel.title: Kanada verhängt Einfuhrverbot für Rinder aus Texas wegen Neuwelt-Schraubenwurmfliege
spiegel.description: Bei zwei Kälbern in Texas sind fleischfressende Parasiten entdeckt worden, die sich leicht verbreiten. Das Nachbarland Kanada verhängt ein Importverbot für Vieh aus dem US-Bundesstaat.

spiegel.title: Drogen, Dreck, Chaos in Berlin: Brennpunkt Kottbusser Tor - SPIEGEL TV
spiegel.description: Drogendealer, Müll und verwahrloste Häuser prägen das Bild des einst lebendigen Kreuzberger Platzes. Die Anwohner wollen ihren »alten« Kiez zurück, das Ordnungsamt hat bei Kontrollen allerhand zu tun.

spiegel.title: Ebola-Ausbruch in Afrika: Diese Impfstoffe gelten als besonders vielversprechend
spiegel.description: In der Demokratischen Republik Kongo grassiert ein Ebolavirus, gegen das es weder Impfstoffe noch Medikamente gibt. Forschende hoffen, schon bald erste Mittel an Menschen testen zu können. Dies sind die Kandidaten.

spiegel.title: Rente und Elterngeld: JU-Chef Johannes Winkel kritisiert Unionskurs
spiegel.description: Die Union sperrt sich gegen höheres BAföG und will das Elterngeld kürzen. Der Vorsitzende der eigenen Nachwuchsorganisation äußert Kritik – und macht einen Gegenvorschlag.

spiegel.title: DFB vor Fußball-WM 2026 in den USA unter Donald Trump: Schweigen, aussitzen, ausweichen
spiegel.description: Selten war eine Weltmeisterschaft so politisch wie in den USA unter Donald Trump. Doch anders als vor vier Jahren in Katar hält sich der DFB extrem zurück. Motto: »Es geht doch nur um Fußball.« Das passt nicht jedem.

spiegel.title: Bushido: Rapper nach Sex im MRT
spiegel.description: Beim Sex bekam er plötzlich heftige Kopfschmerzen: Rapper Bushido berichtet von Ängsten vor einer Hirnblutung. Erst vor einigen Wochen wurde bei ihm ein gutartiger Tumor diagnostiziert.

spiegel.title: Jobcenter: Mitarbeiter nach Kritik in ZDF-Doku entlassen
spiegel.description: Er kritisierte in einer ZDF-Doku das Bürgergeld scharf, dann wurde ihm gekündigt: Der betroffene Jobcenter-Mitarbeiter aus Bremen habe sich nicht konstruktiv geäußert, so die Kommune.

spiegel.title: Tierführerschein: Das Pro und Contra
spiegel.description: Bei falscher Haltung leiden Haustiere. Einige Tierärztinnen wie Christina Bertram fordern daher, dass Menschen vor dem Kauf eine Prüfung ablegen. Ihr Kollege Lothar Hoffmann ist dagegen. Hier sind ihre Argumente.

republika.description: La denuncia sui social di Nicole Ann, turista della Florida: “Ci hanno fatto credere che cannoli e macaron fossero gratis”. Lo scontrino pubblicato online scatena la rabbia degli utenti: oltre 600 commenti

republika.description: La passione per il calcio, l’amore per la Roma e per la fidanzata Matilde. Flavio in finale al Roland Garros

nyt.title: Trump’s Defense Department Sees Growing Espionage Threat From Israel
nyt.description: The Defense Department has increased the counterintelligence threat assessment to its highest level, and Israel is believed to have eavesdropped on American negotiations with Iran.

nyt.title: Israeli Strike Kills 3 Lebanese Soldiers, Days After Truce Was Signed
nyt.description: Israel invaded Lebanon and occupied parts of the country to fight Hezbollah, an Iran-backed armed group, but its military offensive has drawn in others.

nyt.title: Infant Killed as Israeli Military Fires on Car in West Bank, Palestinian Officials Say
nyt.description: Israel’s military said a soldier opened fire after Israeli troops “perceived a vehicle accelerating toward them.” The baby’s grandmother, who was in the car, disputed that account.

nyt.title: As Trump Pushes Deportations, a Skyrocketing Caseload Strains Immigration Courts
nyt.description: A federal surge has more than doubled caseloads within some immigration courts nationwide. Lawyers say the tactic is causing errors and confusion.

nyt.title: Kennedy Center Loses Case Against Musician Who Canceled Over Trump Naming Dispute
nyt.description: A federal judge sided with jazz performer Chuck Redd, who canceled a 2025 holiday concert after President Trump’s name was added to the building.

nyt.title: U.S. Job Market Pushes Past Shocks and Strains
nyt.description: Employers added 172,000 jobs in May, adding to a vigorous pace of hiring in recent months. But wage growth is not keeping up with higher prices and consumers remain pessimistic.

nyt.title: The Bidens Return With New Book and South Dakota Speech Targeting Trump
nyt.description: The re-emergence of the former first family has been fraught for some Democrats who just want to move on.

nyt.title: A.I. Companies Don’t Know What to Do With Alex Bores
nyt.description: Outside groups have spent roughly $12 million to support or oppose Mr. Bores’s campaign for a House seat in Manhattan, elevating his name in a crowded race.

nyt.title: What Are Democrats’ Best Senate Pickup Opportunities?
nyt.description: We’ve grouped six battleground states by some of the factors that shape how likely it is for the party to flip each Senate seat.

nyt.title: Deluged With Mail Ballots, California Takes Its Time Counting Votes Again
nyt.description: Experts say speeding up the count in California would take more resources, but also scaling back rules that expand voting access.

nyt.title: New York City’s Most Patient Soccer Fans Are Ready for the Party
nyt.description: Uzbekistan is new to the World Cup. Norway and Haiti haven’t been there in decades. For expat communities all over the city, the wait is nearly over.

nyt.title: Screwworm Flies Add to Cattle Ranchers’ Woes
nyt.description: Some Texans fear “the nightmares and the horrors” of a potential screwworm outbreak. Elsewhere, not enough grass to feed cattle sends them to market earlier.

nyt.title: Raphael Warnock Says the Supreme Court Has Done ‘Violence’ to Democracy
nyt.description: The Democrat from Georgia on what he sees as the moral issues of our time.

nyt.title: Norma Jeane’s Still Got It!
nyt.description: Some continue to like it hot.

nyt.title: Marco Rubio: Florida Centrist, Tea Party Darling, MAGA Warrior, President?
nyt.description: The secret to the secretary of state’s success.

nyt.description: It was the second such attack in days and came just hours after President Vladimir V. Putin spoke at an economic forum in the city.

npr.title: India's frustrated students find a symbol: the cockroach
npr.description: Young Indians frustrated by unemployment and exam scandals are rallying behind an unusual symbol: the cockroach. NPR's Diaa Hadid reports from New Delhi.

npr.title: Election in Armenia becomes a test of Russian influence
npr.description: Armenia is trying to move closer to Europe and the West, a move that's creating tension with Russia. Journalist Lucy Martirosyan reports from Yerevan ahead of an important election.

npr.title: Israel has reportedly used white phosphorus near Lebanese cities and towns. What is it?
npr.description: White phosphorus is not banned under international law, but can "create cruel injuries" and indiscriminate harm in civilian areas.

npr.title: Israeli airstrikes kill 9 including Lebanese army officers after ceasefire deal
npr.description: The Israeli military confirmed hitting a vehicle and said the incident is being reviewed. Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun called the strike "a flagrant violation to Lebanese sovereignty and international law."

npr.title: Peru is set to elect its 10th president in a decade
npr.description: Peruvians will elect their new president Sunday with polls suggesting a polarized but tight race between hard-right candidate Keiko Fujimori and leftist Roberto Sánchez.

npr.title: U.S. military says it shot down Iranian drones launched toward Gulf allies
npr.description: The exchange of strikes comes as the Trump administration ramps up pressure on Iran to make a deal to end the conflict.

npr.title: Putin promotes a new world economic order at St. Petersburg forum
npr.description: At "Russian Davos," Putin ruled out meeting with Zelenskyy and promoted a new world economic order.

npr.title: Xi Jinping will travel to North Korea next week in first visit since 2019
npr.description: The announcement was made by both countries Friday a day after North Korea unveiled a new facility to produce nuclear fuel.

npr.title: South Africa rolls out game-changing HIV shot amid funding shortfalls
npr.description: A new twice-yearly HIV prevention injection could transform South Africa's fight against the epidemic — but U.S. aid cuts and limited doses threaten to slow its impact.

npr.title: China's highest bridge brings tourists and internet access to remote communities

phys-org.title: Q&A: Why are white-Black marriage rates so low?
phys-org.description: Americans rarely marry outside of their race or class in a nation where residential segregation is relatively common. It is a dynamic widely viewed as a contributing factor to income inequality and intergenerational social mobility.

phys-org.title: 120,000-year-old European fallow deer—tracing the loss of genetic diversity
phys-org.description: European fallow deer have faced a dramatic loss of genetic diversity since the last interglacial period. This was revealed by 120,000-year-old fossils from central Germany's Neumark-Nord site in Saxony-Anhalt, analyzed by researchers from the University of Potsdam, the MONREPOS Research Center and Museum in Neuwied, and Leiden University. phys-org.title: Ever seen a cave cricket? Australia now has three new species of these spindly, spider-like creatures
phys-org.description: When you picture a cave, you probably think of an environment devoid of life. But for most caves on Earth, this couldn't be further from the truth.

phys-org.title: Infrastructure for African mines destroying forests at 34 times the rate of the mines themselves
phys-org.description: Industrial-scale mining in Africa to support global supply chains is leading to unprecedented deforestation across the continent, with 34 hectares of forest removed for every single hectare of active mine site.

phys-org.title: AI-generated compounds hit specific cell types and outperform conventional screening
phys-org.description: The classical drug discovery paradigm begins with a known molecular target: a protein whose modulation is expected to reverse the course of a disease. However, in many pathologies, such a target does not always exist or is not sufficiently characterized.

phys-org.description: Chloromethane is a gas that is toxic to humans and contributes to the depletion of the ozone layer. It is produced during the combustion of coal, biomass and other raw materials. Natural sources such as algae, plants and fungi also release it. This system converts the gas into nontox

phys-org.title: Mount Etna eruptions reveal carbon dioxide and water can trigger separate explosive paths
phys-org.description: The plumbing systems of volcanoes are vast and complex. But they aren't consistent, even in the same volcano. A Cornell-led collaboration found very different mechanisms behind two historic eruptions of Mount Etna in Italy. Understanding these dynamics—combined with the techniques that revealed them—can help geologists assess the risk of future eruptions.

phys-org.title: Africa's climate crisis is a legal crisis too: What are states' duties under human rights law?
phys-org.description: A landmark climate case is being heard by the African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights. The request was brought by the Pan African Lawyers Union and other African civil society organizations. They've asked the court to issue advice on what responsibilities African governments have to protect their countries against the climate crisis and move away from an economy that harms the environment.

phys-org.title: Predictive surrogates could cut quantum computing measurement overhead by more than 99.97%
phys-org.description: Quantum computers, systems that process information leveraging quantum mechanical effects, have the potential of outperforming classical computers on some tasks. Despite their potential, the use of these systems remains very limited, due to their high cost and other challenges that have so far prevented their large-scale fabrication.

phys-org.title: Sweet basil carbon dots show potential for sustainable agriculture
phys-org.description: What if a common herb found in the kitchen could help farmers grow healthier crops? As the global population grows and agriculture faces increasing environmental challenges, scientists are searching for innovative ways to improve crop productivity while reducing reliance on chemical inputs.

phys-org.title: Smart surfaces face zero gravity test in boiling heat experiments
phys-org.description: A research team led by Davoud Jafari at the University of Twente, in collaboration with the University of Pisa, has completed a series of parabolic flight experiments to investigate advanced smart surfaces under rapidly changing gravity conditions. Conducted aboard the Air Zero G aircraft operated by Novespace, the campaign integrated additive manufacturing, boiling heat transfer and electric field control into a single experimental platform as part of the #SmartSkin project.

phys-org.title: MUSE maps spiral galaxy W2246f, uncovering old core and ongoing star formation across disk
phys-org.description: Astronomers have employed the Multi-Unit Spectroscopic Explorer (MUSE) on the Very Large Telescope (VLT) to perform deep spectroscopic observations of a peculiar spiral galaxy known as W2246f. Results of the observational campaign, published May 27 on the pre-print server arXiv, offer new insights into how this galaxy evolved and shed more light on its nature.

phys-org.title: NZ's new forestry rules promise consistency: Will they also increase environmental risk?
phys-org.description: One of the most important changes to New Zealand's environmental regulations in recent years came into force this week. Yet outside policy circles, the forestry sector and a handful of councils, few people are likely to have noticed.

phys-org.title: Hair-size microrobots combine three cancer-fighting functions in preclinical animal tests
phys-org.description: Imagine a future where cancer treatment affects only the tumor, where eye injections are no longer required and brain surgeries don't result in large incisions or long recovery times. That's the future researchers at Michigan State University are working toward.

phys-org.title: Canada's aerial wildfire‑fighting plan is a start—but it is not yet a strategy
phys-org.description: The Canadian government recently announced that it will lease a fleet of 10 firefighting aircraft and other support assets to be deployed for the 2026 wildfire season. The plan will see these 10 leased aircraft being managed by the Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Center deployed strategically across the country and made available to provinces as they face intense wildfires.

phys-org.title: Volcanic eruptions linked to rising famine risk across China's history
phys-org.description: Large volcanic eruptions may have played a bigger role in triggering historical famines across China than previously understood, according to a new study that traced links between eruptions, climate disruption, and food shortages over more than four centuries.

phys-org.title: Green space exposure, mental health and the nasal microbiome explored
phys-org.description: Plenty of studies have linked exposure to nature to a wide variety of health benefits, from improved cognitive function to lower blood pressure to better mental health. Other research has found connections between the human microbiome and time spent outside. But an overlooked, understudied player in that connection is the assemblage of microbes found in the nose, or the nasal microbiome.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
proj-syn.description: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.

proj-syn.title: When Markets Run on Empty
proj-syn.description: Markets are flying high despite geopolitical turmoil because a broad-based willingness to keep spending has been matched by an ability to keep doing so. But as more economic participants exhaust their means and rely on debt, a painful moment of truth will arrive—sooner rather than later if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

proj-syn.title: The Pope and the AI Profiteers
proj-syn.description: In his first encyclical, Pope Leo XIV rightly rejects the idea that markets alone can be trusted to shape society’s technological future. Recognizing that AI raises questions that prices and profits cannot answer, the Chicago-born pope has posed a direct challenge to Chicago School economics.

proj-syn.title: AI Must Not Encroach on Human Dignity
proj-syn.description: In a world captivated by technological advances, Pope Leo XIV’s first encyclical seeks to shift attention away from the marvels and terrors of AI and toward the magnificence of humanity. The message that the technology lacks a “moral conscience” and is distinct from human cognition is necessary and welcome.

proj-syn.title: The Key Forces Now Shaping Markets and Geopolitics
proj-syn.description: Three major factors are likely to shape economic and geopolitical outcomes over the next several years: politically unconstrained AI development, a shift from the logic of globalization to zero-sum thinking, and heightened international tail risks. Much could go right, or at least as expected—until it doesn’t.

proj-syn.title: The Living Ghosts of Violent Radicalism
proj-syn.description: Following World War II, the most militant student movements emerged in the former Axis powers as a way to cope with previous generations' complicity. But while the Red Army Faction and others were haunted by memories of past crimes, today's young people have mostly forgotten, and a growing number think far-right politics are cool.

proj-syn.title: Using AI to Test Policy Language
proj-syn.description: Policymakers have long understood that language affects economic behavior, but until recently, there were few tools capable of systematically analyzing its effects. AI may now help close that gap, enabling officials to anticipate how framing and timing can move markets and shift public opinion.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Competitiveness Bogeyman
proj-syn.description: Calls for European leaders to protect domestic industry from "unfairly" subsidized Chinese competition have lately grown louder. But while tariffs might offer temporary relief to a few sectors, they cannot restore Europe's technological leadership, industrial dynamism, or export competitiveness.

proj-syn.title: Putting American Science on a MAGA Leash
proj-syn.description: A draft rule from US President Donald Trump’s White House Office of Management and Budget would subject all scientific research funding to the whims of political appointees, further undercutting a pillar of American power. The goal is to foreclose any future that is plural, contestable, and beyond the president’s control.

proj-syn.title: How Measles Came Roaring Back
proj-syn.description: Bangladesh is facing soaring measles cases not because of a single localized failure, but because of years of systemic erosion. Ultimately, maintaining herd immunity against highly contagious viruses requires relentless attention to supply and demand, as well as to the broader social and institutional foundations of public health.

proj-syn.title: Pete Hegseth’s Dangerous Call to Arms in Asia
proj-syn.description: Much like it did in Europe, the Trump administration has called on US allies in the Indo-Pacific to increase military spending to 3.5% of GDP. But a defense buildup on this scale would jeopardize economic growth and regional unity, and could lead Southeast Asian countries to gravitate toward China’s strategic orbit.

proj-syn.title: The Pope’s AI Vision and Its Limits
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical on AI is clear-eyed about the limits of techno-utopianism. But its vision of technology directed toward human flourishing needs to be extended to include the interests of every sentient being, human and nonhuman, biological or—possibly—artificial.

proj-syn.title: The Iran War Is Fueling a Global Debt Shock
proj-syn.description: Once again, a global crisis is disproportionately burdening countries that did not cause it. Across the Global South, the food- and energy-price shock triggered by the conflict in the Middle East has morphed into a debt shock that demands an urgent international response.

proj-syn.title: Democracy vs. Data Centers
proj-syn.description: As tech companies race to build data centers, communities and lawmakers across the United States are pushing back. Industry leaders frame local opposition as a threat to American competitiveness, but China’s experience shows that unchecked expansion carries serious risks of its own.

proj-syn.title: The Right Incentives for Climate Action
proj-syn.description: As the closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to disrupt global oil and gas flows, countries are increasingly focusing on short-term energy priorities to the detriment of long-term decarbonization goals. In such a context, the difficult task of designing climate policies that realign incentives takes on new importance.

proj-syn.title: The US and India Have Become Regional Rivals
proj-syn.description: While the US views India as a counterweight to China in Asia, it balks at the idea of Indian regional dominance, preferring a pluralistic order. The Trump administration has gone further by pursuing close ties with Pakistan, apparently hoping that the US and India can remain global partners.

proj-syn.title: Digital Sovereignty Is in the Fine Print
proj-syn.description: Despite efforts to build their own digital industries and infrastructure, most countries remain dependent on American tech firms for the provision of core government services. But government officials can tip the balance of bargaining power by attaching certain standardized provisions to public procurement and services contracts.

proj-syn.title: Trump Wants to Privatize His Presidential Records
proj-syn.description: By enacting the Presidential Records Act in response to Richard Nixon’s malfeasance, the US Congress created a process to limit abuse of power and ensure accountability. Like Nixon, Donald Trump seems determined to avoid accountability, which has led his Justice Department to argue—poorly—that the PRA is unconstitutional.
